name: Torii Security Group Compact Combat Shotgun TSS-3 'Chorus'
description:
A compact combat shotgun in the Torii Security Group TSS-3 line — a commercial Tier 3 offering sold through licensed distributors in GLMZ and across the Pulse network. The TSS-3 is not a bespoke weapon: it is a production model, available by order, priced accordingly. What makes Kyle’s unit distinctive is the bird’s-head grip — a sharply recurved grip profile without a stock, giving the weapon the silhouette of a large revolver at the cost of extended-range control. The bird’s-head configuration ships as a factory option on the TSS-3; Kyle ordered it specifically for one-handed operation. At 48cm total, it disappears under a coat.

The barrel is cut to the GLMZ compact firearm legal minimum. The action cycles reliably one-handed. The chamber and feed ramp are factory-treated for adverse conditions — blood-slicked hands, wet environments, extreme cold. The magazine accepts four rounds of 12-gauge. The grip texture is Torii’s signature red-line crosshatch. The bird’s-head curves sharply backward — the back of the grip nearly parallel to the barrel line — so the hand sits under the bore rather than behind it. This places the recoil directly up the wrist rather than rotating the muzzle. You can hold it on target through the blast.

The name Chorus was Kyle’s. The katana is Silence. The shotgun is what follows Silence when Silence was not enough.
tier_availability: Tier 3 — commercial production. Available by order through Torii Security Group licensed distributors. Bird’s-head grip configuration is a factory option, not a custom modification.
legality: Legal — GLMZ compact firearm classification. Requires Tier 2 commercial arms license, available to corporate employees and licensed contractors.
street_price: Φ 3,200 base model; Φ 3,800 with bird’s-head grip option and adverse-condition chamber treatment
specifications:
caliber: 12-gauge
capacity: 4+1 rounds
effective range: Contact to 15 meters
barrel length: 360mm (legal minimum)
overall length: 480mm (stock folded) / 720mm (stock extended)
weight: 2.1kg unloaded
action: Semi-automatic, gas-operated
grip: Bird’s-head configuration (factory option) — no stock, sharply recurved
finish: Matte black ceramic-composite chassis, dark steel action, red-line crosshatch grip texture
tactical_use: Close-quarters companion to the katana. Deployed when the blade reaches a threshold it cannot cross — armored targets, entrenched opponents, multiple close contacts. Designed for one-hand operation so the katana can remain in the other hand. Four rounds means four choices. Kyle reportedly fires it rarely and considers each shot a failure of planning.
cultural_context: The shotgun occupies an interesting philosophical position in Kyle's loadout: the katana is his identity, his discipline, the thing he chose. The shotgun is an admission. That there are situations the blade cannot solve, that sometimes the elegant answer isn't available, that the world doesn't arrange itself around the weapon you prefer. That Kyle carries it at all — a concession his character doesn't make easily — says something about how seriously he has learned to take being alive.
story_hooks: Someone breaks into The Pivot and finds the TSS-3 in a locked case — Chorus engraved in small letters along the barrel. They know immediately whose place this is, and that whoever lives here was prepared for situations a katana can't handle.

Kyle fires Chorus for the first time in a year. One shot. The sound is unmistakable in the enclosed space where the fight happens. Everyone who hears it knows something went wrong enough that the blade wasn't the answer.
Torii Security Group's armorer knows exactly who commissioned this weapon and what they've done with it. They've been watching.

physical_description.visual_profile: Compact and undecorated. Matte black ceramic-composite chassis with no stock — the bird’s-head grip curves sharply backward under the receiver, giving the weapon a silhouette closer to a large revolver than a shotgun. The Torii red-line grip texture runs along the bird’s-head curve and the abbreviated forend. At first glance it reads as a sidearm until you see the bore diameter. The Chorus marking is minimal: small, clean, milled into the receiver.
physical_description.weight_description: 2.1kg unloaded. Designed to be carried. Heavy enough to feel real, light enough not to remind you it's there.
physical_description.primary_material: Ceramic-composite chassis over steel action. Same material specification as the TSK-1 katana components.
physical_description.finish: Matte black throughout. No reflective surfaces. Red accent line in grip texture — the only color.
physical_description.color_scheme: Black with red accent. Minimal. Intentional.
physical_description.grip_texture: Bird’s-head configuration — sharply recurved grip without stock. Hand sits below and behind the bore rather than behind it; recoil travels up the wrist rather than rotating the muzzle. Torii red-line crosshatch texture on the full grip surface.
distinctive_features: Bird’s-head grip — no stock, sharply recurved, sidearm-profile silhouette
Red-line Torii crosshatch texture on bird’s-head grip and forend
Chorus milled into receiver in small clean lettering
480mm total length — conceals under a standard coat
Chamber and feed ramp treated for adverse conditions including blood-slick
Action cycling tuned for reliable one-hand operation
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Small TSG logo on receiver. 'TSS-3' designation. 'Chorus' milled into left side of receiver.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained. Shows careful use — clean action, no cosmetic wear from casual handling. Kyle treats it like a tool he respects but doesn't enjoy.
